title: 2004 AMC 10A Problem 14
statement: The average value of all the pennies, nickels, dimes, and quarters in Paula’s purse is \(20\) cents. If she had one more quarter, the average value would be \(21\) cents. How many dimes does she have in her purse?

solutions.text:
With \(n\) coins the total value is \(20n\) cents. Adding a quarter gives \[ 20n + 25 = 21(n + 1), \] so \(n = 4.\)

If there were at most two quarters, the other coins would be worth at most \(10\) cents each, so four coins would total at most \(2(25)+2(10)=70\) cents. Thus there must be three quarters, leaving \(5\) cents for the fourth coin. The purse contains three quarters and one nickel, so it has \(0\) dimes.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: If she has \(n\) coins, their total value is \(20n\) cents
